injuries.description: Left thumb being almost completely amputated by the saw.
source: his left thumb being almost completely amputated by the saw.

manifestations.description: Complete numbness over that part of the left thumb distal to the cut wound.
Residual numbness at the palmar aspect of the left index and middle fingers.
Complete loss of motion in the interphalangeal joint of the left thumb.
Overall range of movement of the left index, middle and ring fingers was satisfactory despite a very mild loss in the end range of extension.
Sensitive spot over the donor site of the nerve graft (tender spot).
A neuroma developed at the distal end of the nerve at the donor site for the nerve graft.
With the residues in the left hand the plaintiff might not be able to perform the carpentry work in full capacity and would likely perform activities with reduced speed and efficiency.

treatments_received: Emergency operation (same day) with fusion of the left thumb interphalangeal joint
Revascularization of the radial digital artery
Repair of the radial digital nerve
Repair of the nail bed of the little finger
Physiotherapy (34 sessions between May and November 2000)
Two further nerve grafting operations (first in October 2000, second about half a year later)
K-wires removal at Duchess of Kent Children's Hospital

losses.description: Scarring and neuroma (tender spot) at the donor site and scarring related to the hand injuries.
Might not be able to perform carpentry work in full capacity; activities likely performed with reduced speed and efficiency.
